newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-FORGET RETIRES AFTER 15 YEARS ON CIRCUIT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FORGET RETIRES AFTER 15 YEARS ON CIRCUIT.

text.p: France's Guy Forget said on Friday he was retiring from competitive tennis after 15 years on the circuit.
"It was not an easy decision to make. I still felt at times I could recover," said the 32-year-old, who has battled numerous injuries since turning professional in 1982.
Forget reached a career-high singles ranking for four in the world in 1991, advancing to the quarter-finals at Wimbledon on three occasions.
"I could not keep training four hours a day," Forget said, adding he would play his last singles tournament in France in October.
Born in Morocco before his parents settled in Marseille, Forget secured the decisive rubber in France's Davis Cup victory over the United States in 1991.

The same year, he won six ATP titles, including the Paris Open with a win over Pete Sampras in the final. His favourite tournament was the Toulouse Open, an event which his father and grandfather had won before him and which he took three times.
Forget was also one of the best doubles players on the circuit, winning 28 titles, most of them with Swiss Jakob Hlasek.
